covers: the blank-read gate: rows make a result usable, a zero-transaction statement is usable when a balance came back, a blank read is not usable, and a non-mapping is not usable
the model opening winning over its own opening row, and an opening row filling in when the model omitted the opening
a blank date inheriting the previous one, a row with money but no date kept, and a pure noise row dropped
confidence downgraded when both sides are missing or when the balance is missing, and an unknown confidence word becoming high
the printed footer totals kept as numbers or nulled
ledger rows merged across chunks, a failed chunk not sinking the others, the opening only coming from the first chunk, rows without a date dropped, and the account filter applied
no usable ledger rows being a failure, and an unreadable account code not being listed
the statement prompt version and the ledger prompt hint
only rows the chain refused being counted as breaks
a non-PDF never triggering a reread, and no breaks meaning no rendering and no pages read
an implausible page count being skipped, and the page limit being the caller's choice
a reread with fewer breaks adopted, with the escalation record checked field by field
a reread that is not better thrown away, including two pages that each look fine but break the chain once joined
one failing page discarding the whole round (a half reread loses rows)
the pages being read in order over the given range

checks.note: the pinned functions are executed with the devices replaced by fakes (model client, upgrade policy, caches, page splitter, renderer, page reader, thread-pool wrapper) because those are the parts this batch does not port. Statement rows are compared field by field including confidence and the deduplication fingerprint, plus the opening, closing, bank code and printed totals, and the failure text when the read is blank. The reread comparison covers the adopted rows by fingerprint and the whole escalation record. The prompt texts are compared byte for byte: the statement prompt is pulled out of the pinned function body by AST, the ledger template is compared directly, and gl_prompt is compared with the deployed .format call for three account codes.

intentional_differences: the model client and its upgrade policy (json_from_pdf, try_with_fallback, flash_lite) are not ported: the model call is injected by the caller, which is how this platform's engine already takes it. The statement gate is therefore applied by the caller, exactly where the deployed policy applied it
the in-memory LRU and the on-disk cache are not ported, but the prompt version string (v63-totals) is kept because it is part of what the prompt means: changing the prompt must invalidate old results
the PDF devices (page count probing, page splitting, page rendering) are not ported; page_count and read_page(page_number) are injected instead

the thread pool, the cost-attribution wrapper, the environment switches and every log line are not ported: the ported arbitration reads the pages in order and the size cap is a parameter defaulting to the deployed 50
the private helper names became public entries because the engine wiring in the next batch consumes them; every judgement and every returned string is the deployed one
the exceptions the deployed module swallows (returning ok=False with the exception text) are left to the caller: a pure module does not decide how a failure is reported
not_run: wiring the prompts, the model-result handling or the reread into any caller — the engine document tier and the execution wiring are the next batch
